description: What do you do when an adoption agency lies or misrepresents the background of a child you adopt? Is there a legal solution? Wrongful Adoption in Georgia.
shortAnswer: Courts have recognized a duty to disclose known relevant information about a child's health and social background to prospective adoptive families. In the face of a breach of this duty to disclose, courts have held agencies liable for Wrongful Adoption and awarded adoptive families monetary compensation.

faq.q: What do adoptive parents have to prove in a Wrongful Adoption claim?
faq.a: The adoptive parents must show they were wronged by adoption agencies that failed to provide their child's full background information, and that in failing to disclose (or misrepresenting facts about the child), the agency deprived them of the chance to make an informed decision. The parents must also show that they suffered financially, physically, or emotionally.

faq.q: Can a Georgia family sue an adoption agency for breach of contract or under RICO?
faq.a: In Cesnik v. Edgewood Baptist Church, 88 F.3d 902 (C.A.11 (Ga.), 1996), the court allowed a breach of contract action in the Wrongful Adoption context and also allowed the wronged family to maintain federal and Georgia RICO claims. The RICO statutes allow not only for compensatory damages but also treble damages, punitive damages, attorney fees and expenses of litigation.

faq.q: If we signed a waiver or notice of risk with the adoption agency, do we have no case?
faq.a: Such waiver and notices may shield an agency from certain legal liabilities. But exercising the proper duty of care may not be contracted away by the agency. There is always grounds for challenging a waiver that excuses an agency from behaving in a prudent and reasonable manner.

faq.q: How long do you have to file a Wrongful Adoption claim in Georgia?
faq.a: In Cesnik v. Edgewood Baptist Church, the court indicated that the deadline on Wrongful Adoption claims (at least so far as the tort claim goes) is probably 2 years from the date of the agencies wrongful acts. If you miss the deadline you lose all your rights with regard to that particular claim.
